overview_subtitle: {host} · live via Podman socket and D-Bus

overview_alert_stateFailed: The unit is in state failed.
overview_services_detected: discovered automatically from Caddy and Quadlets, plus your own links

overview_metrics_retention: Saved every 30 s, kept for 7 days. Gaps: Quadeck was not running at the time.

overview_chart_empty: No data in this time range yet.
overview_dialog_iconsOffline: Icon collection not available offline – enter the slug directly (e.g. “home-assistant”).

timers_editor_descriptionPlaceholder: Copy photos to the backup disk
timers_editor_persistent: Catch up on missed runs (server was off)
timers_editor_deleteBody: Timer and service are stopped and both unit files are removed.
timers_schedule_vendor: The timer comes from a package – its file stays untouched.

timers_schedule_modified: (The files were changed by hand, so only the schedule can be adjusted here.)

quadlets_list_pick: Select a file on the left.
quadlets_compose_startUnits: Start the units after creating them
quadlets_editor_otherEntries: Other entries stay unchanged (edit them in the text view):

quadlets_editor_deleteBody: {unit} will be stopped and the file deleted. It is kept in the history.
quadlets_history_diffNote: Difference between this version and the current state in the editor:
quadlets_history_load: Load this version into the editor

podman_fields_logdriver_help: journald: container logs in the journal (recommended).
podman_fields_tz_help: “local” uses the time zone of the host.
podman_config_missing: not present yet – Podman uses the defaults from /usr/share/containers
podman_config_saveNote: Checked as TOML before writing. Applies to newly started containers.
podman_updates_introMiddle: pulls new images for containers with
podman_updates_noTimer: podman-auto-update.timer is not present on this system.
podman_all_on: AutoUpdate=registry now applies to all containers

podman_all_unsupported: Needs Podman 5 or newer (installed: {version}). Until then, set AutoUpdate=registry per file.

disks_smart_readAt: Read {when} · automatically every 30 minutes, sleeping drives are not woken up
disks_smart_notInstalled: smartctl is not installed – without the smartmontools package Quadeck cannot read the SMART values of the drives.
disks_smart_historyKept: History values are stored hourly and kept for one year.

disks_card_longStarted: Long self-test started on {name} (several hours; the drive stays usable)
disks_card_standbyText: The drive is asleep – it is not woken up for SMART. Values on the next read while it is active.
disks_card_unsupportedText: {msg} – normal for virtual drives; for USB enclosures one with SAT support often helps.
disks_detail_noHistory: No history yet – values are stored hourly.
disks_detail_errorCountersTitle: Error counters – rising values are the warning sign
disks_mounts_introBefore: Which disks are mounted where at boot ({path}). Every change is checked first – device, file system, driver,
disks_mounts_introAfter: , systemd's fstab generator and a test mount with the chosen options. System entries are left untouched.
disks_mounts_noEntries: No data disks in the fstab yet.
disks_mounts_allIncluded: All file systems are in the fstab.
disks_mounts_mountedNotInFstab: · currently mounted at {at}, but not in the fstab – gone after a reboot
disks_mounts_blocksBootTitle: If the disk is missing at boot, the server stops in emergency mode. “nofail” prevents that.
disks_mounts_uuidHelp: With the UUID the entry stays correct even if sdb becomes sdc after a rebuild.
disks_mounts_nofailHelp: If it is missing or broken, the server boots anyway.
disks_mounts_nofailWarn: Without nofail the server stops in emergency mode at boot if the disk is missing.
disks_mounts_automountHelp: The boot does not wait for the disk; it is mounted when first opened.
disks_mounts_harden: Harden as a pure data disk (nodev, nosuid)
disks_mounts_hardenHelp: Device files and setuid programs on the disk are ignored.
disks_mounts_roHelp: Nothing on the disk can be changed.
disks_mounts_compressHelp: New files are compressed transparently – saves space, costs some CPU.
disks_mounts_fatHelp: {fs} has no Linux permissions – owner and permissions apply to all files:
disks_mounts_wouldBlock: This entry would block the boot if the disk is missing – you have to confirm that explicitly when saving.
disks_mounts_checked: Checked – a test mount follows when saving.
disks_mounts_installPackage: Install the package: System → Installed, or
disks_mounts_rollback: If a step fails after writing, Quadeck restores the previous fstab.
disks_mounts_confirmCritical: {targets} has no “nofail”: if the disk is missing at boot, the server stops in emergency mode and is only reachable again after intervention at the console. I want it this way anyway.
files_page_subtitle: Files in the data areas – copy, move, rename, delete
files_explorer_noRoots: No data areas found (/mnt, /srv, /media, /home, /data). Add your own with QUADECK_FILE_ROOTS.
files_explorer_deleteBody: Folders are deleted with all their content. There is no trash.

shares_smbDialog_usersPlaceholder: empty = all Samba users, e.g. tristan @family
shares_smbDialog_passwordHint: Samba users need their own password:
shares_nfsDialog_syncTitle: sync: confirm only once on disk (safer)

match.hasAur=*: Packages via {manager} · container images via podman auto-update

system_updates_unreadNews: There is unread Arch news – please read it first.

match.nPlural=other: {helper} builds {n} packages as {user}. PKGBUILDs are not shown – only update packages you trust.

system_updates_imagesBody: {names} are restarted with the new image (podman auto-update, with rollback).
system_packages_protectedHint: Protected system package – cannot be removed here.

match.nPlural=other: {n} packages will be removed – the selected ones and dependencies nothing else needs:

system_packages_blocked: Protected packages would be affected ({names}) – removal is blocked.
system_config_intro: An update brought a new version but did not overwrite your changed one.
system_config_hint: Compare, then keep yours, take over the new one or merge both. On the console the same works with {cmd}.
system_config_binary: Not a text file or too big – only delete or keep here.
system_config_diffIntro: Difference from your version ({minus}) to the new one from the package ({plus}):
system_config_noLive: {live} does not exist – the new version:
system_config_mergeIntro: Your version to edit – take over what you need from the new one (see the difference above). Exactly this text is saved.
system_config_mkinitcpio: Then the initramfs is rebuilt (mkinitcpio -P) – as a job with output.
boot_reloadsWhenBack: The page reloads as soon as it is reachable again. That usually takes one to two minutes.

match.hasEntry=*: Containers and services are shut down cleanly and start again afterwards.

boot_jobRunning: “{title}” is running right now – better wait.
boot_grub: GRUB – Quadeck only shows the kernel parameters here; GRUB manages entries and the default itself.
boot_kernelHint: Several kernel variants can be installed side by side; use “Boot this once” to switch back and forth.
boot_dkmsHint: DKMS modules (e.g. NVIDIA, ZFS) are built for every kernel with the matching headers.
boot_paramsSd: in the {options} line of the entry under {dir} or in {cmdline}
boot_newFileText: – a copy of the default entry with the same parameters, only kernel and initramfs swapped. Existing entries stay unchanged.
boot_removeKernelBody: Removes the package {pkg} (and the headers, if installed) with pacman. The boot entry then points nowhere and can be removed here.
boot_startsOnceAfter: . The reboot after that uses the default again – if something goes wrong, a reset is enough.
boot_firmwareStays: The server stays in the firmware menu until someone on site continues – it is not reachable over the network then.
boot_allStopped: All containers and services are stopped. The server is unreachable for one to two minutes, Quadeck included.
boot_jobAborted: “{title}” is still running and would be aborted.
hardware_copyHttps: Copying only works over https or localhost – please select the text
hardware_vmUnavailable: not available or turned off in the BIOS
hardware_slotsUnreadable: Slots not readable (dmidecode missing or virtual machine).
hardware_eccYes: yes – memory errors are detected and corrected
hardware_gpuHint: With this line in the [Container] section of the Quadlet, Jellyfin or Immich, for example, use the GPU for hardware transcoding.
hardware_usbHint: The path under /dev/serial/by-id stays the same even when ttyUSB0 becomes ttyUSB1 after a reboot – enter it like this in Home Assistant or Zigbee2MQTT (AddDevice= in the Quadlet).
hardware_noSensors: No sensors readable (normal in VMs; otherwise the kernel module is often missing, e.g. nct6775 or it87).
network_subtitle: Interfaces, routes, DNS, open ports, firewall and reverse proxy
network_fw_blocked_title: The firewall does not let connections from outside through
network_fw_podman_title: Podman opens published container ports itself
network_firewall_noFirewall: No firewall active: everything listening on “all interfaces” is reachable in the local network. Behind a router this is common at home – from outside only what the router forwards gets through.
network_firewall_blocked: , but blocked: {ports}. Intended? Otherwise allow it in the firewall (e.g.
proxy_intro: Domains that Caddy forwards to containers and services. Nothing is saved before Caddy has checked it; then Caddy loads the new config without interruption.
proxy_status_api: Caddy is running – changes via the admin API
proxy_status_container: Caddy is running in the container {c}
proxy_table_also: Also in the Caddyfile: {parts} – editable as text only.
proxy_table_unstructured: The Caddyfile is not organised in blocks (e.g. a single site without braces) – editable as text only.
proxy_pick_hint: Absolute path on the server, e.g. /home/tristan/docker/caddy/Caddyfile. Quadeck remembers it; QUADECK_CADDYFILE takes precedence.
proxy_pick_envHint: The path comes from QUADECK_CADDYFILE (/etc/quadeck/quadeck.env) and can only be changed there.
proxy_site_domainsHint: Separate several with commas. Caddy gets the HTTPS certificate itself – the domain must point to this server.
proxy_site_targetHint: Address where Caddy reaches the service, e.g. localhost:8096. Suggestions: containers with a published port.
proxy_text_revision: Version from {date} – save to restore it
proxy_confirm_steps: Caddy checks the new version, then {path} is saved (the previous one goes to the history) and Caddy is reloaded. If Caddy rejects it, everything stays as it is.
proxy_confirm_stopped: Caddy is not running: the file is saved and read at the next start.
proxy_done_api: Saved – Caddy loaded the new config
proxy_done_container: Saved – Caddy reloaded in the container
proxy_done_automatic: The Caddyfile is found automatically again
proxy_errors_badAddress: “{a}” is not a valid address (e.g. app.example.com or :8080)
proxy_errors_badTarget: “{u}” is not a valid target (e.g. localhost:8096 or jellyfin:8096)
proxy_errors_custom: {a} has its own settings – please edit it as text
proxy_errors_fileName: The file name must contain “Caddyfile” (e.g. Caddyfile or sites.caddyfile)
proxy_errors_envMissing: QUADECK_CADDYFILE points to {p}, there is no file
proxy_errors_json: {q} starts Caddy with a JSON config – Quadeck cannot edit that
proxy_errors_notMounted: {q} does not mount {inside} from the host – the file is inside the image, changes would be gone with the next start. To edit it, add to the Quadlet: Volume=/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:{inside}
proxy_errors_mountedMissing: {q} mounts {p}, but there is no file
proxy_errors_notFound: No Caddyfile found – no Caddy Quadlet with a mounted Caddyfile, no caddy.service and no /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.
proxy_errors_notText: {p} is not a text file or too big
proxy_errors_unchecked: Not checked: Caddy is not running and cannot be started here – the file will be read the next time Caddy starts.
proxy_errors_changed: The Caddyfile was changed in the meantime – please reload and make the change again.
proxy_errors_rejected: Caddy rejects the file – nothing changed:
proxy_errors_reloadFailed: Reload failed – the old file is restored, Caddy keeps running unchanged:
proxy_errors_stopped: Saved. Caddy is not running – the change applies from the next start.
ssh_subtitle: Access to the server: keys, hardening, logins
ssh_install_what: No SSH server installed – without it the server can only be reached directly with screen and keyboard.
ssh_access_enabled: SSH now also starts at boot
ssh_access_fingerprints: Fingerprints of this server – compare them when connecting for the first time
ssh_hardening_passwordOnHelp: Bots keep trying passwords. Turn it off as soon as your key works.
ssh_hardening_passwordOffHelp: Good: login only with an added key.
ssh_hardening_rootYesHelp: Risky: root with password. Better log in as a normal user and use sudo.
ssh_hardening_rootOtherHelp: root cannot get in with a password.
ssh_hardening_allowedHelp: Optional: only these accounts may log in via SSH.
ssh_hardening_noKeys: No user has a key yet – add one first.
ssh_hardening_noInclude: sshd_config does not include sshd_config.d/*.conf – settings can only be applied here after adding “Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf”.
ssh_logins_none: No logins in the last 30 days (or no access to the journal).
ssh_logins_failedHint: As long as password login is on, these attempts have a chance – turn it off or set up fail2ban.
ssh_newDevice_step1: Create a key on the new device (once):
ssh_newDevice_step2Password: as long as password login is on, this works directly:
ssh_newDevice_step2Key: Paste the content of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub above under “Keys” (password login is off, so ssh-copy-id does not work).
ssh_newDevice_step3: Connect and, the first time, compare the fingerprint with “Access” above:
ssh_keys_none: No key yet – {name} can only log in with a password.
ssh_preview_force: I can reach the server another way (screen/keyboard, IPMI) and want this anyway.
users_subtitle: Accounts on the server – login, password, groups, SSH keys, Samba
users_detail_adminHelp: May use sudo and unlock Quadeck.
users_login_noPassword: no password – login only with an SSH key
users_login_nothing: Neither password nor key – nobody can log in with this account.
users_login_sambaNone: no Samba password yet – shares can only be accessed as guest
users_password_sambaHelp: Only applies to access to shares (SMB) and is independent of the login password.
users_password_mismatch: The two entries do not match
users_create_mismatch: The two passwords do not match

match.admin=true: The account gets no password. You add the public key afterwards in the details – as administrator it still needs a password for sudo and to unlock Quadeck.
match.admin=*: The account gets no password. You add the public key afterwards in the details.

notifications_subtitle: The server lets you know when something is wrong – on your phone or in the chat
notifications_channels_none: No channel yet – without a channel nothing is sent. Easiest: install the ntfy app, make up a topic, enter it here.
notifications_channels_removeBody: Nothing will be sent to this channel anymore.

match.recovery=true: Each problem is reported once; when it is resolved, an all-clear follows.
match.recovery=*: Each problem is reported once; when it is resolved, no further message follows.

notifications_rules_recovery: Send an all-clear when a problem is resolved
notifications_security_none: none (only a relay in your own network)
notifications_email_fromHelp: Most providers require your own address here.
notifications_dialog_topicHelp: On ntfy.sh anyone who knows the name can subscribe to a topic – so pick a name that is hard to guess.
ui_Timers_sunMonTueWedThu: Sun Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat

ssh_lastWorkingKeyPasswordLogin: This is the last working key and password login is off – afterwards nobody could get onto the server via SSH.
ssh_noSshServiceInstalledPackage: No SSH service installed (package openssh or openssh-server)
ssh_noKnownKeyTypeExpected: No known key type (expected e.g. “ssh-ed25519 AAAA… name@device”)
ssh_keyDataMissingNotBase64: Key data missing or not Base64
ssh_keyDataDoesNotMatch: Key data does not match the type {type}
ssh_dsaNoLongerAcceptedBy: DSA is no longer accepted by current OpenSSH
ssh_rsaBitsTooShortToday: RSA with {bits} bits – too short today, better ed25519
ssh_pleaseAddKeysOptionsFrom: Please add keys with options (from=, command= …) by hand
systemd_belongsQuadeckItselfNotChanged: {unit} belongs to Quadeck itself and is not changed here
systemd_systemdOnlyChecksTemplateUnits: systemd only checks template units as an instance – syntax checked only
systemd_belongsQuadeckItselfChangesHere: Belongs to Quadeck itself – changes here could lock Quadeck out
systemd_transientUnitSystemdRunDisappear: Transient unit (systemd-run) – disappears when it ends
systemd_notChangePackageFilesOverride: {path} is not in {dir} – change package files with an override
systemd_symlinkWillNotOverwritten: {path} is a symlink and will not be overwritten
systemd_savedButDoesNotRestart: Saved, but {unit} does not restart: {value} – see the journal
systemd_nameLettersDigitsSuffixLike: Name: letters, digits, - _ . and a suffix like .service
systemd_createdButStartFailedSee: Created, but the start failed: {value} – see the journal
systemd_notChangePackageFilesOverride2: {path} is not in {UNIT_DIR} – change package files with an override
timers_actionMustRunEnableDisable: Action must be run, enable or disable
timers_alreadyExistsPleaseChooseAnother: {u} already exists – please choose another name
timers_wasNotCreatedByQuadeck: {name} was not created by Quadeck and is not deleted here
timers_timerAlreadyExistsPleaseChoose: {name}.timer already exists – please choose another name
users_rootSystemAccountNotDeleted: root is the system account and is not deleted
users_accountLoggedProcessesRunningUnder: The account is logged in or processes are running under it – log out or stop them first
users_nameAlreadyExistsMaybeAs: The name already exists (maybe as a group)
boot_hideMenuPressKeyAt: Hide the menu (press a key at boot to see it)
boot_alwaysWaitUntilSomeonePicks: Always wait until someone picks one
boot_installedButHasNoBoot: {pkg} is installed but has no boot entry – “Create boot entry”
boot_onlyLeftKernelInitramfsNeeds: Only {free} left on {path} – a kernel with initramfs needs {needed}. The next kernel update can fail and leave the server unbootable: remove old kernels or fallback images.
boot_systemdBootEspOlderThan: systemd-boot on the ESP ({espVersion}) is older than the installed systemd ({packageVersion}) – “Update boot loader” (bootctl update).
boot_noDefaultEntryFoundSystemd: No default entry found – systemd-boot then takes the first one in the list.
boot_optionsMountingEGBtrfs: Options for mounting / (e.g. the btrfs subvolume)
boot_mountSystemWritableRightAway: Mount the system writable right away
boot_mountSystemReadOnlyFirst: Mount the system read-only first (fsck checks it before)
boot_encryptedPartitionUnlockedAtBoot: Encrypted partition that is unlocked at boot
boot_initramfsLoadedAlongKernel: initramfs loaded along with the kernel
boot_onlyShowKernelMessagesUp: Only show kernel messages up to level {value}
boot_hardwareWatchdogOffBitFaster: Hardware watchdog off – a bit faster, but no automatic restart on hangs
boot_protectionAgainstCpuVulnerabilities: Protection against CPU vulnerabilities (Spectre & co.) turned off – faster, but less secure
boot_intelGpuLoadGucHuc: Intel GPU: load GuC/HuC – needed for hardware transcoding (QuickSync) in Jellyfin, Plex, Immich
boot_intelGpuArcXeForce: Intel GPU (Arc/Xe): force the new xe driver
boot_intelGpuForceDriverCards: Intel GPU: force the driver for cards not yet officially supported
boot_amdGpuPowerOverclockingFeatures: AMD GPU: power and overclocking features
boot_nvidiaKernelModeSettingNeeded: NVIDIA: kernel mode setting (needed for Wayland and some containers)
boot_usbPowerSavingOffHelps: USB power saving off – helps against USB disks that drop off
boot_suspendUsbDevicesAfterMany: Suspend USB devices after this many idle seconds
boot_nvmePowerSavingStatesOff: NVMe power saving states off – helps against SSDs that vanish under load
boot_nvmeDeepestAllowedPowerSaving: NVMe: deepest allowed power saving state
boot_forcePciePowerSavingEven: Force PCIe power saving (even where the BIOS does not report it)
boot_pciePowerSavingLevelPowersupersave: PCIe power saving level (powersupersave saves the most)
boot_iommuPassDevicesThroughVms: IOMMU on – pass devices through to VMs (VFIO)
boot_amdIommuPassDevicesThrough: AMD IOMMU – pass devices through to VMs
boot_reserveThesePciDevicesVms: Reserve these PCI devices for VMs
boot_blankConsoleScreenAfterS: Blank the console screen after {value} s
boot_whereKernelMessagesGoScreen: Where kernel messages go (screen, serial port)
boot_compressedCacheFrontSwap: Compressed cache in front of swap on
boot_cgroupsVersion1V2Only: cgroups version (1 = v2 only, as Podman needs it)
boot_showStatusUnitsAtBoot: Show the status of units at boot
boot_messagesUdevInitramfs: Messages of udev in the initramfs
boot_showStatusUnitsInitramfs: Show the status of units in the initramfs
boot_reserveFixedNumberHugePages: Reserve a fixed number of huge pages
boot_amdCpuFrequencyScalingVia: AMD CPU: frequency scaling via CPPC (active usually saves more)
boot_operatingSystemReportedBiosWorkarou: Operating system reported to the BIOS (workaround for firmware bugs)
boot_acpiResourcesLaxSensorsSome: ACPI resources (lax: sensors of some mainboards become readable)
boot_forceSettingsSataPortsE: Force settings for SATA ports (e.g. speed)
boot_trustCpuSRandomNumbers: Trust the CPU’s random numbers at boot
boot_noGraphicsModeSettingOnly: No graphics mode setting – only for troubleshooting, turns off hardware acceleration
boot_rebootSAfterKernelPanic: Reboot {value} s after a kernel panic
boot_kvmIgnoreUnknownCpuRegisters: KVM: ignore unknown CPU registers (Windows VMs)
boot_splitLockDetectionOffSome: Split lock detection (off: some games, VMs faster)
boot_runningRightNowBootAnother: Running right now – boot another kernel first
boot_defaultEntryMakeAnotherKernel: Is the default entry – make another kernel the default first
configfiles_newVersionDoesNotKnow: The new version does not know your users – taking it over would delete every account except root. Almost always: “Keep mine”.
configfiles_holdsPasswordsNeverTakeOver: Holds the passwords – never take over the package version.
configfiles_newVersionDoesNotKnow2: The new version does not know your groups and memberships.
configfiles_groupPasswordsNeverTakeOver: Group passwords – never take over the package version.
configfiles_listsAllowedShellsNewVersion: Lists the allowed shells; the new version does not know ones installed later (zsh, fish). Usually “Keep mine”.
configfiles_holdsYourDisksPackageVersion: Holds your disks – the package version would drop them from boot.
configfiles_mistakeHereLocksSudoOnly: A mistake here locks sudo – only change it by hand with visudo.
configfiles_holdsYourOwnNamesPackage: Holds your own names; the package version is empty.
configfiles_settingsSshServerKeepYour: Settings of the SSH server. Keep your changes (Port, password login, AllowUsers) – Quadeck’s own live in sshd_config.d/ and stay anyway. sshd -t checks the file before saving.
configfiles_buildsInitramfsKernelStartsS: Builds the initramfs the kernel starts with. Be sure to keep your MODULES and HOOKS lines (encryption, btrfs, GPU, plymouth) – otherwise the server will not boot. Rebuild the initramfs afterwards.
configfiles_presetKernelSInitramfsRebuil: Preset for a kernel’s initramfs. Rebuild the initramfs afterwards.
configfiles_settingsPacmanCarryOverYour: Settings of pacman. Carry over your own changes: [multilib], ParallelDownloads, Color, IgnorePkg, your own repositories.
configfiles_listDownloadServersIfYou: List of download servers. If you did not maintain it yourself (or generate it with reflector), the new version can be taken over – but then uncomment at least one server.
configfiles_whichLocalesGeneratedKeepYou: Which locales are generated. Keep your uncommented lines (e.g. de_DE.UTF-8), otherwise run locale-gen afterwards.
configfiles_yourSharesDefinedHereNever: Your shares are defined here – never simply take over the package version. testparm checks the file before saving.
configfiles_settingSystemdServicePackage: Setting of a systemd service. The package version is usually all commented out; your own values are better placed in a drop-in (…conf.d/).
configfiles_settingsBuildingPackagesAurC: Settings for building packages (AUR). Carry over your own values (MAKEFLAGS, COMPRESSZST), otherwise take the new version.
configfiles_loginRulesPamCarefulMistakes: Login rules (PAM). Careful: mistakes here can prevent logins. If you changed nothing, take over the new version.
configfiles_settingsPodmanKeepYourRegist: Settings of Podman. Keep your registries and storage locations.
configfiles_settingsGrubKeepYourGrub: Settings for GRUB. Keep your GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX line; run grub-mkconfig afterwards.
configfiles_profilesTpmWithoutChangesYou: Profiles for the TPM. Without changes of your own, the new version can be taken over.
configfiles_savedVersionRemovedPackageNo: Saved version of a removed package – not in use. If you need nothing from it, it can go.
configfiles_replacedByNewVersionYour: {live} is replaced by the new version; your previous one is kept as {live}.quadeck-bak.
configfiles_deletedStaysAs: {path} is deleted; {live} stays as it is.
configfiles_savedYourEditedTextPrevious: {live} is saved with your edited text (previous version as {live}.quadeck-bak), {path} is deleted.
configfiles_yourLinesDifferFromNew: Your {list} lines differ from the new version (e.g. sd-encrypt, btrfs, GPU modules). Taking it over could leave the server unbootable – please “Merge” and keep your lines.
configfiles_newVersionDoesNotContain: The new version does not contain your shares ({list}) – taking it over would delete them. “Keep mine” or merge.
fstab_tooFewFieldsAtLeast: Too few fields – at least source and mount point
fstab_fieldsFstabHasAtMost: {length} fields – fstab has at most 6 (write spaces in paths as \040)
fstab_fstabHasBeenChangedMeantime: The fstab has been changed in the meantime – please reload
fstab_mountPointMustAbsolutePath: The mount point must be an absolute path (/mnt/…)
fstab_givePathWithoutDoubleTrailing: Give the path without “.”, “..”, double or trailing “/”
fstab_controlCharactersNotAllowedPath: Control characters and “#” are not allowed in the path
fstab_systemDirectoryUseEG: {path} is a system directory – use e.g. /mnt/name or /srv/name
fstab_sourceGiveUuidLabelPartuuid: Source: give UUID=…, LABEL=…, PARTUUID=… or /dev/…
fstab_fileSystemEGExt4: File system: e.g. ext4, xfs, btrfs
fstab_quadeckDoesNotKnowOption: Quadeck does not know option “{o}” for {vfstype} – the test mount shows whether the driver accepts it
fstab_roRwAtSameTime: ro and rw at the same time
fstab_noautoAutomountMountedAccessOnly: noauto with automount: mounted on access only
fstab_checkOrder1MeantData: Check order 1 is meant for / – data disks 2 or 0
fstab_notCheckedFsckAtBoot: {vfstype} is not checked with fsck at boot – set field 6 to 0
fstab_alreadyLineMountPointMay: {file} is already in line {prev} – a mount point may appear only once
fstab_noEntryUnusual: No entry for / – that is unusual
fstab_systemEntryWouldChangedRemoved: A system entry would be changed or removed: {gone}
fstab_newSystemEntryNotAllowed: A new system entry is not allowed: {added}
hardware_runsAtXInsteadX: runs at x{linkWidth} instead of x{maxLinkWidth}
hardware_usuallySlotHasFewerLanes: {who} {link} – usually a slot that has fewer lanes or shares them with another one (see the mainboard manual).
hardware_linkedAtInsteadOftenCable: {disk}{value} is linked at {speed} instead of {limit} – often the cable or port; matches CRC errors in SMART.
hardware_biosFromNewerVersionsOften: The BIOS is from {year}. Newer versions often fix bugs and security holes – check the mainboard maker’s website.
hardware_runsVirtualMachineSlotsSensors: Runs in a virtual machine ({virt}) – slots, sensors and links then show the virtual hardware.
ini_lineNeitherSectionKeyValue: Line is neither a section, Key=Value nor a comment
ini_setMoreThanOnceLast: {key} is set more than once – the last value applies (line {line})
notify_systemdUnitContainerServiceState: A systemd unit or a container service is in the state “failed” – e.g. the nightly backup.
notify_httpCheckTileOverviewHas: The HTTP check of a tile on the overview has been failing for over 2 minutes.
notify_healthcheckReportsUnhealthyContai: Healthcheck reports “unhealthy” or a container without a unit has crashed (over 2 minutes).
notify_warningCriticalStateAccordingSmar: Warning or critical state according to the SMART evaluation.
notify_onceDayNewPackagesContainer: Once a day: new packages and container images – only if something changed since the last message.
notify_pushYourPhoneViaNtfy: Push to your phone via ntfy.sh or your own ntfy server: pick a topic and subscribe to it in the ntfy app.
notify_yourOwnGotifyServerCreate: Your own Gotify server: create an app in Gotify and enter its token.
notify_createBotBotfatherEnterToken: Create a bot with @BotFather, enter the token, write to the bot and enter the chat ID (e.g. via @userinfobot).
notify_postJsonUrlWorksDiscord: POST with JSON to a URL – works for Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Home Assistant or your own scripts.
notify_viaSmtpServerYourMail: Via the SMTP server of your mail provider. Gmail, GMX, web.de and the like often need a separate app password for this, not the normal password.
notify_appPasswordAtMyaccountGoogle: App password at myaccount.google.com → Security (2-factor must be on)
notify_onlySendPasswordEncryptionSsl: Only send a password with encryption (SSL/TLS or STARTTLS)
notify_recipientsOneMoreEMail: Recipients: one or more e-mail addresses (comma-separated)
notify_killedByKernelLackMemory: killed by the kernel for lack of memory
notify_eMailGoesViaSmtp: E-mail goes via SMTP, not HTTP
notify_sentByQuadeckChangeNotifications: Sent by Quadeck. Change notifications: Quadeck → Notifications.
shares_rootDirectoryCannotShared: The root directory cannot be shared
shares_nameLettersDigitsSpacesMax: Name: letters, digits, spaces, “_ . - $”, max. 80 characters
shares_usersNamesGroupSeparatedBy: Users: names or @group, separated by spaces
shares_clientIpNetwork192168: Client “{host}”: IP, network (192.168.1.0/24), host name or *
shares_rwRoAtSameTime: {host}: rw and ro at the same time
smart_driveItselfReportsImminentFailure: The drive itself reports an imminent failure
smart_preFailureAttributeBelowIts: A pre-failure attribute is below its threshold now
smart_preFailureAttributeWasBelow: A pre-failure attribute was below its threshold in the past
smart_errorsDriveSErrorLog: Errors in the drive's error log
smart_transferErrorsCrcUsuallyCable: transfer errors (CRC) – usually cable or backplane
smart_newTransferErrorsCrcSince: {added} new transfer errors (CRC) since {value} – {count} in total; check cable or backplane
smart_olderTransferErrorsCrcNone: {count} older transfer errors (CRC), none new since {value} – the counter is never reset, only an increase would be a problem
smart_transferErrorsCrcSinceInstallation: {count} transfer errors (CRC) since installation – the counter is never reset; Quadeck will tell you as soon as new ones appear
smart_getReplacementBackUpYour: Get a replacement and back up your data – the drive shows wear or defects.
smart_checkReplaceSataCablePower: Check or replace the SATA cable and power connector; the drive itself is often fine. The CRC counter then stops but does not go back – if it no longer rises, the problem is fixed.
smart_improveCoolingAirflowFansSpacing: Improve cooling (airflow, fans, spacing between the drives).
smart_smartctlCannotReadDriveUsb: smartctl cannot read the drive – USB enclosure without SAT support or missing permissions.
ssh_allowedUsersNamesSeparatedBy: Allowed users: names separated by spaces
timers_commandContainsControlCharactersT: Command contains control characters or is too long
timers_workingDirectoryMustAbsolutePath: Working directory must be an absolute path
timers_monTueWedThuFri: Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun
timers_systemdDoesNotSupportSteps: systemd does not support steps for weekdays
timers_rebootNotScheduleUnitWantedby: @reboot is not a schedule – a unit with WantedBy=multi-user.target fits better
timers_cronNeedsFiveFieldsMinute: Cron needs five fields: minute hour day month weekday
timers_cronRunsWhenDayWeekday: Cron runs when the day OR the weekday matches – systemd requires both. Please check.
unitFiles_onlyAddsOverrideReplaceInsert: {key}= only adds in an override – to replace, insert an empty {key}= line before it
unitFiles_noSectionUnitNeedsAt: No [Section] – a unit needs at least [Unit] or [Service]
units_oomKillMemoryLimitMemorymax: OOM kill: memory limit MemoryMax={value} reached
units_oomKillTerminatedByKernel: OOM kill: terminated by the kernel due to low memory
units_timedOutWhileStartingStopping: Timed out while starting or stopping
units_tooManyRestartsShortTime: Too many restarts in a short time (start limit)
units_resourcesMissingEGImage: Resources missing (e.g. image, volume or network)
users_readJournalAllServices: Read the journal of all services
users_nameLowercaseLettersDigitsStarting: Name: lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (starting with a letter), at most 32 characters
users_fullNameNoColonComma: Full name: no colon, comma or line break
users_afterwardsNobodyCouldLogAs: Afterwards nobody could log in as administrator anymore – Quadeck could not be unlocked and sudo would no longer work. Give another administrator a password first.
users_setsNewPasswordRunningSessions: Sets a new password for {name}. Running sessions stay logged in.
users_locksNoMoreLoginsNot: Locks {name}: no more logins, not even with an SSH key. Running sessions and services of the account keep running.
users_setsSambaPasswordNetworkShares: Sets the Samba password of {name} (for network shares, separate from the login password).
quadletKeys_C_Image: Image, preferably fully qualified (docker.io/…), otherwise AutoUpdate=registry does not work.
quadletKeys_C_ContainerName: Name of the container (default: systemd-<file name>).
quadletKeys_C_Volume: Mount a volume or directory: source:target[:options]; .volume files as name.volume.
quadletKeys_C_Network: Network: host, none, a Podman network or a .network file (name.network).
quadletKeys_C_AutoUpdate: registry: podman auto-update pulls new images; local: only locally built ones.
quadletKeys_C_Exec: Arguments for the command in the image (replaces CMD).
quadletKeys_C_User: User in the container (UID or name).
quadletKeys_C_UserNS: User namespace, e.g. keep-id or auto.
quadletKeys_C_HealthOnFailure: Action when unhealthy: none, kill, restart, stop.
quadletKeys_C_Pod: Pod (.pod file) the container runs in.
quadletKeys_C_IP: Static IPv4 address in the network.
quadletKeys_C_IP6: Static IPv6 address in the network.
quadletKeys_C_Timezone: Time zone, e.g. local or Europe/Berlin.
quadletKeys_C_NoNewPrivileges: No new privileges in the container.
quadletKeys_C_Pull: Pull policy: always, missing, never, newer.
quadletKeys_C_Rootfs: Root file system instead of an image.
quadletKeys_C_ServiceName: Override the name of the systemd unit.
quadletKeys_POD_ExitPolicy: Behaviour when all containers have exited.
quadletKeys_NET_NetworkName: Name of the Podman network (default: systemd-<file name>).
quadletKeys_VOL_VolumeName: Name of the volume (default: systemd-<file name>).
quadletKeys_VOL_Copy: Copy the content of the image into the volume.
quadletKeys_IMG_ImageTag: Name the image is referenced by.
quadletKeys_SYSTEMDKEYS_Requires: Start these units too; if one fails, this one stops as well.
unitKeys_UNIT_After: Start only after these units (e.g. network-online.target).
unitKeys_UNIT_Requires: Start these units too; if one fails, this one stops as well.
unitKeys_UNIT_ConditionPathExists: Only start if the path exists (e.g. a mounted disk).
unitKeys_SERVICE_Type: simple: runs permanently · oneshot: script that exits · notify/forking: as the program requires.
unitKeys_SERVICE_ExecStart: Command with full path. In an override, set an empty ExecStart= first.
unitKeys_SERVICE_EnvironmentFile: File with variables (leading -: may be missing).
unitKeys_SERVICE_TimeoutStartSec: How long the start may take, e.g. 90s or infinity.
unitKeys_SERVICE_MemoryMax: Memory limit, e.g. 2G – above it the kernel kills the service.
unitKeys_SERVICE_CPUQuota: CPU limit, e.g. 50% (of one core) or 200%.
unitKeys_SERVICE_ProtectSystem: Read-only system: full = /usr, /boot, /etc · strict = everything except allowed paths.
unitKeys_SERVICE_ProtectHome: Hide home directories or make them read-only.
unitKeys_TIMER_OnCalendar: Schedule, e.g. *-*-* 03:00:00 or Mon..Fri 07:30. In an override, set an empty OnCalendar= first.
unitKeys_TIMER_OnUnitActiveSec: Repeat this long after the last start, e.g. 1h.
unitKeys_INSTALL_WantedBy: Start at boot: multi-user.target (services) or timers.target (timers).
fstab_option_defaults: Default settings (rw, suid, dev, exec, auto, nouser, async).
fstab_option_nofail: If the disk is missing at boot, the server boots anyway – without this option it ends up in emergency mode.
fstab_option_xsystemddevicetimeout: How long systemd waits for the disk at boot (default 90 s).
fstab_option_noauto: Do not mount at boot, only by hand or on demand.
fstab_option_xsystemdautomount: Mount on first access only – the boot does not wait for the disk.
fstab_option_xsystemdidletimeout: With automount: unmount again after this much idle time (the disk may sleep).
fstab_option_xsystemdmounttimeout: Maximum time for the mount itself.
fstab_option_xsystemdrequires: Mount only once this unit is running.
fstab_option_xsystemdmakefs: Format an empty device at boot – careful.
fstab_option_xmountmkdir: Create the mount point if it is missing.
fstab_option_xgvfsshow: Show in the desktop file manager.
fstab_option_netdev: Needs the network – mount only after it is up.
fstab_option_noatime: Do not write access times – fewer writes, disks sleep longer.
fstab_option_relatime: Update the access time only rarely (default).
fstab_option_lazytime: Keep timestamps in memory only and write them in batches.
fstab_option_users: Any user may mount and unmount.
fstab_option_owner: The owner of the device may mount.
fstab_option_group: The group of the device may mount.
fstab_option_exec: Programs on the disk may run (default).
fstab_option_noexec: Do not run programs from this disk.
fstab_option_nosuid: Setuid bits are ignored – safer for data disks.
fstab_option_nodev: Device files are ignored – safer for data disks.
fstab_option_discard: TRIM on every delete – for SSDs the weekly fstrim.timer is usually better.
fstab_option_errors: On errors: continue, remount-ro or panic.
fstab_option_commit: Write to the disk every this many seconds.
fstab_option_data: Journal mode: ordered, writeback or journal.
fstab_option_nobarrier: Without write barriers – only with a battery-backed cache.
fstab_option_inode64: Create inodes anywhere on the disk (default).
fstab_option_allocsize: Size reserved in advance when writing.
fstab_option_compress: Compress new files, e.g. zstd or zstd:3.
fstab_option_compressforce: Always compress, even poorly compressible files.
fstab_option_spacecache: Free space cache, v2 is the default.
fstab_option_degraded: Mount even with a disk missing from the RAID.
fstab_option_uid: Owner of all files (user ID) – this file system has no Linux permissions.
fstab_option_umask: Permissions that are removed, e.g. 022 (others may only read) or 002.
fstab_option_iocharset: Character set of the file names, e.g. utf8.
fstab_option_flush: Write earlier – safer for removable media.
fstab_option_windowsnames: Do not create names Windows cannot open.
fstab_option_prealloc: Reserve space in advance when writing – less fragmentation.
fstab_option_force: Mount even if Windows marked the disk as “dirty”.
fstab_option_credentials: File with user name and password.
fstab_option_soft: If the server fails, return an error instead of waiting.
fstab_option_x: Option for systemd or other programs (ignored by the kernel).
boot_flavor_linux_text: Latest stable version – the default kernel of Arch.
boot_flavor_linuxlts_text: Long-term kernel, rarely changes – the classic way back when an update of linux causes trouble.
boot_flavor_linuxzen_text: Tuned for short response times – more for desktops and gaming.
boot_flavor_linuxhardened_text: With extra hardening; some programs do not run with it.
users_describe_withoutPassword: , without password – login only with an SSH key

match.admin=true: Saves name, shell and groups of {name} (administrator via {group}). New groups apply from the next login.
match.admin=*: Saves name, shell and groups of {name}. New groups apply from the next login.

match.removeHome=true: Deletes {name} along with the home directory and mail spool – the files will be gone.
match.removeHome=*: Deletes {name}; the home directory is kept.

match.isDefault=true: “{title}” points to missing files ({files}) – the server will not boot with this entry. It is the default entry!
match.isDefault=*: “{title}” points to missing files ({files}) – the server will not boot with this entry (e.g. after removing a kernel – remove the entry)

match.canInstall=true: Only one kernel installed. A second one (e.g. linux-lts) is a way out if a kernel update causes trouble – then “boot linux-lts once”. Install it below under “Kernel”.
match.canInstall=*: Only one kernel installed. A second one (e.g. linux-lts) is a way out if a kernel update causes trouble – then “boot linux-lts once”.

ssh_noInclude: {file} does not include sshd_config.d/*.conf – add “Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf” at the top

match.password=true: Saved, but sshd uses different values (password login on, root {root}) – another file in sshd_config.d or sshd_config sets them first.
match.password=*: Saved, but sshd uses different values (password login off, root {root}) – another file in sshd_config.d or sshd_config sets them first.

match.hasPackage=true: Driver for {type} is missing – install package {pkg}

declarations: local gib = value: number minimumFractionDigits=1 maximumFractionDigits=1
